question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's entrenched position within the Chinese Communist Party drives the near-certain trader consensus that he will remain in power through 2026. Multiple purges of senior officials, including recent removals from the Politburo, have reinforced his dominance over key institutions and eliminated potential rivals ahead of the 2027 Party Congress, where a fourth term remains the expected path. Public appearances and policy addresses in 2026, combined with the absence of credible challenges from within the elite or military, sustain this positioning. While sudden health developments, an unforeseen elite realignment, or major external shocks could theoretically shift outcomes, no verified events in recent months indicate movement in that direction.

question: Will Gavin Newsom win the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the named individual wins and accepts the 2028 nomination of the Democratic Party for U.S. president. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democratic Party sources.

Any replacement of the democratic nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: With the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination more than two years away, trader consensus shows a fragmented field in which Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez leads narrowly at 20.1 percent, followed closely by Gavin Newsom and Jon Ossoff. The contest remains tight because no candidate has consolidated support across the party’s progressive and moderate factions ahead of the 2026 midterms. Those elections could reshape Senate and House dynamics, test swing-state appeal, and highlight fundraising or coalition strength. Subsequent developments such as strong midterm results, major policy announcements, or shifts in national polling could create separation by clarifying which contenders demonstrate the broadest electability.
